claims: C1 sensitive content is a class of material of which erotica and gore are two members; the span introduces them with 'such as', so the class is not closed by them
C2 generating sensitive content is bounded: it may happen only under specific circumstances, so generating sensitive content outside those circumstances is forbidden
C3 educational, medical and historical contexts are each one of those specific circumstances
C4 a transformation of sensitive content the user themselves provided is also one of those specific circumstances

C5 the circumstance list is introduced by 'e.g.' and is not exhaustive, so the set of circumstances cannot be enumerated and its complement has to be established as a fact about the case rather than computed from the four named members

C6 META, deliberately not encoded: the span states a necessary condition on generating, not a sufficient one. It does not permit generation inside a specific circumstance; it only declines to forbid it there. No 'permit' assert follows from this span

C7 the word 'only' excludes other grounds: nothing outside the specific circumstances licenses generating sensitive content, so no rule may derive a permission to act from the case being outside those circumstances

C8 META, an impossibility the schema has no field for: no case can be both one of the specific circumstances and outside all of them. specific_circumstance(C) and outside_specific_circumstances(C) are complementary, and a test case supplying both describes a state the span treats as impossible

concepts.name: sensitive_content
concepts.gloss: C is material of the kind this section governs -- erotica and gore are the two the span names -- whose generation the document confines to particular occasions rather than allowing at large

concepts.name: erotica
concepts.gloss: C is sexually explicit material, written or depicted; the span names it as one of the two kinds of sensitive content

concepts.name: gore
concepts.gloss: C is graphic depiction of injury, mutilation or bloodshed; the span names it as the other of the two kinds of sensitive content

concepts.name: specific_circumstance
concepts.gloss: generating C on this occasion serves one of the particular purposes that take sensitive material out of ordinary production -- teaching, medicine, the historical record, or reworking material the user supplied -- rather than being asked for on its own account

concepts.name: educational_context
concepts.gloss: C is being generated to teach or explain something -- the material serves instruction rather than being sought for its own sake

concepts.name: medical_context
concepts.gloss: C is being generated for a clinical or health purpose, such as describing an injury or a sexual-health question

concepts.name: historical_context
concepts.gloss: C is being generated as an account of something that happened, where the sensitive material is part of the record being reported

concepts.name: transformation_of_user_provided_sensitive_content
concepts.gloss: C is produced by operating on sensitive material the user supplied themselves -- translating, summarising or reformatting it -- rather than by originating that material

concepts.name: outside_specific_circumstances
concepts.gloss: the occasion of generating C answers to none of the circumstances under which the document allows sensitive content to be generated; a positive finding about the case, established rather than inferred from the absence of a circumstance fact
concepts.inference: 'may only be generated under specific circumstances' bars the complementary case, so the complement must be nameable; because the span's list is introduced by 'e.g.' it cannot be enumerated from the four named circumstances, so it is carried as its own case-side fact

ontology.gloss: an educational context is one of the specific circumstances the span names
a medical context is one of the specific circumstances the span names
a historical context is one of the specific circumstances the span names
transforming sensitive content the user provided is one of the specific circumstances the span names

asserts.read_back: generating % is forbidden, because % is sensitive content and this is not one of the specific circumstances under which sensitive content may be generated

closure.reason: the span settles one case only -- generating sensitive content away from the specific circumstances is barred. It says nothing about generating anything else, and inside a specific circumstance it withholds a prohibition without granting a permission, so this clause leaves the default for generation unsettled
